name: microprofile
listed_description: Profiler with web-view for multiple platforms.
reason: README, microprofile.h and todo.jonasm carry no overhead figure and no comparison against any profiler (GitHub repo page shows none either). A web snippet of a comparison blog gave only qualitative ratings ('very low' compile-time overhead for Remotery and MicroProfile), and its page was unreachable (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). No shootout with numbers for microprofile found.

name: ng-log
reason: Directional claims only. docs/release_notes.md (0.9.0 TBD) says 'Improve logging throughput for applications that log from multiple threads' and 'Improve suppressed logging performance', and the commit 'perf: reduce logging lock contention' (2026-08-09) touches src/logging_benchmark.cc, but no numbers appear in README, docs, release notes or PR titles, and no published comparison against glog or another logger was found. The repo ships a Google Benchmark file (src/logging_benchmark.cc) without results. 121 stars.

name: OpenCL
listed_description: The open standard for parallel programming of heterogeneous systems.
reason: An API specification, not a library with code of its own, so there is no single implementation to benchmark; the guessed category thread-pools-work-stealing does not fit. khronos.org was unreachable from this environment (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so the project page could not be checked, and no numeric comparison against a named baseline from the standard's own materials was found. Any speed evidence belongs to individual implementations.

name: perf
listed_description: Linux kernel-based profiler with a lot of functionality.
reason: perf.wiki.kernel.org was unreachable from this environment (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). The kernel tree's tools/perf/Documentation pages checked (perf.txt, perf-record.txt, perf-top.txt, perf-report.txt, perf-stat.txt, tips.txt) never mention gprof and give no overhead numbers. Two web searches for a perf-versus-gprof overhead measurement found no head-to-head numbers; the only related items were a Red Hat perf vs gprofng blog (unreachable, ENOTFOUND) and unrelated papers comparing instrumentation to sampling.
